title: Proper hypercover descent for nearby cycles
statement: Let $S$ be Noetherian, $f:X\to S$ of finite presentation, and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring killed by an integer invertible on $S$. Let $\epsilon:Y_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial scheme whose augmentation and simplicial matching maps are proper surjective, with every $Y_i$ of finite presentation over $S$. For $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ with $H^j(K)=0$ for $j<c$, put $f_i=f\epsilon_i$ and $K_i=\epsilon_i^*K$, and write $\bar\epsilon_i:V_{f_i}\to V_f$ for the induced maps. In the notation of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] there is a cohomological descent spectral sequence $E_1^{i,j}=H^j(R\bar\epsilon_{i,*}R\Psi_{f_i}K_i)\Longrightarrow H^{i+j}(R\Psi_fK)$, with $i\geq0$ and $j\geq c$. For each total degree $n$, the abutment has a finite filtration whose associated graded sheaves are the $E_\infty^{i,n-i}$ for $0\leq i\leq n-c$. The spectral sequence and its augmentation are natural for base changes of $S$.

source.place: Section 9.2, printed p. 22, displayed proper-hypercover descent identity and associated spectral sequence.

proof.text: Use the total etale topos of $Y_\bullet$ and the total topos of the simplicial vanishing topoi $V_{f_i}$. These are the family categories with componentwise coverings in [lem-trf-total-site-augmentation-spectral-sequence]. The exact pullback $\epsilon^*K$ has component $K_i$. The maps $\psi_{f_i}:Y_{i,\mathrm{Et}}\to V_{f_i}$ assemble to a total morphism $\psi_\bullet$, and the $\bar\epsilon_i$ assemble to an augmentation $\bar\epsilon$. Indeed, the projection descriptions and the canonical identifications $\bar\epsilon_i\psi_{f_i}\simeq\psi_f\epsilon_i$ in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] commute with every face and degeneracy: both composites have the same two projections and the same oriented $2$-morphism, so the universal property gives their unique compatible identifications. Thus $\bar\epsilon\psi_\bullet\simeq\psi_f\epsilon$.

source.place: General simplicial-site total construction and component functoriality; Orgogozo Section 9.2, p. 22, the simplicial vanishing topos.

proof.text: The matching-map assumptions are exactly those of [def-trf-proper-hypercover]. Apply [lem-trf-proper-hypercover-etale-descent] to $K$ on $X$. It is bounded below, and the coefficient ring is annihilated by the stated integer. The ordinary adjunction unit therefore gives $K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\epsilon_*\epsilon^*K$. The descent assertion requires neither properness of $f$ nor any goodness condition on nearby cycles.

Put $L=R\psi_{\bullet,*}\epsilon^*K$. The component assertion of [lem-trf-total-site-augmentation-spectral-sequence] and the definition $R\Psi_{f_i}=R\psi_{f_i,*}$ give $r_iL\simeq R\Psi_{f_i}K_i$. All these module-sheaf categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. Exact constant-coefficient inverse image preserves the bound $c$ on $K_i$. Left t-exactness [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] applied to each direct image gives $H^j(r_iL)=0$ for $j<c$. Exactness and joint conservativity of component restriction then give $H^j(L)=0$ for $j<c$.

Using the commuting total square of Step 1, apply derived direct-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] on its two sides. Together with the isomorphism of Step 2 this gives
$$R\bar\epsilon_*L\simeq R\bar\epsilon_*R\psi_{\bullet,*}\epsilon^*K\simeq R\psi_{f,*}R\epsilon_*\epsilon^*K\simeq R\Psi_fK.$$
The augmentation in the opposite direction $R\Psi_fK\to R\bar\epsilon_*L$ is $R\psi_{f,*}$ applied to the ordinary descent unit, followed by the displayed composition identifications. These identifications use the composite-adjunction normalization of [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization]; hence this specifies the canonical augmentation, rather than merely an isomorphism of its source and target.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; derived.tex Tag 09T5 for adjunction normalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-total-site-augmentation-spectral-sequence] to $\bar\epsilon$ and $L$, using the bound proved in Step 3. Substitution of $r_iL=R\Psi_{f_i}K_i$ identifies its first page with $H^j(R\bar\epsilon_{i,*}R\Psi_{f_i}K_i)$ and Step 4 identifies its abutment with $H^{i+j}(R\Psi_fK)$. This gives the requested spectral sequence, with horizontal degree $i\geq0$, vertical degree $j\geq c$, and alternating-face first differential.

The same general-site theorem supplies the filtration: for $n\geq c$ it is $F^0H^n=H^n$, $F^{n-c+1}H^n=0$, with $F^iH^n/F^{i+1}H^n\simeq E_\infty^{i,n-i}$. The possible indices are exactly $0\leq i\leq n-c$. For $n<c$, the abutment is zero and the filtration is the zero filtration. Thus each degree uses finitely many columns even when the vertical complexes have no uniform upper bound.

source.place: Tag 0D7F, bounded-below alternating-face double complex and first-quadrant convergence.

proof.text:
Let $g:S'\to S$ be any base change, and prime all the families and topoi. The proper hypercover remains a proper hypercover by [lem-trf-proper-hypercover-etale-descent]. Write $v:V_{f'}\to V_f$ and $w:V_{f'_\bullet}\to V_{f_\bullet}$. The ordinary comparison for the total nearby-cycle square gives $w^*L\to L'$. Functoriality of [lem-trf-total-site-augmentation-spectral-sequence], first for the augmented square and then for this coefficient map, gives a morphism from $v^*$ of the old spectral sequence to the primed one. Its first-page map is the composite
$$v^*R\bar\epsilon_{i,*}R\Psi_{f_i}K_i\longrightarrow R\bar\epsilon'_{i,*}v_i^*R\Psi_{f_i}K_i\longrightarrow R\bar\epsilon'_{i,*}R\Psi_{f'_i}K'_i,$$
on cohomology. The second arrow is the comparison $\beta$ defined in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] for $Y_i$: the component identifications of [lem-trf-total-site-augmentation-spectral-sequence] are the canonical base-change maps, so restricting the total mate $w^*L\to L'$ to component $i$ and pasting it with those base-change squares by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (clauses 1 and 2) gives the mate of the component square $v_i\psi_{f'_i}\simeq\psi_{f_i}h_i$ for $h_i:Y'_i\to Y_i$, which is $\beta$. With the composition normalization of Step 4, mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] identifies the abutment map with $v^*R\Psi_fK\to R\Psi_{f'}K'$ and makes the augmentation square commute: pasting across $\bar\epsilon\psi_\bullet\simeq\psi_f\epsilon$ yields the same inverse-image square, hence the same mate. This proves base-change naturality, including composition of base changes. These are comparison maps; no assertion that they are isomorphisms is used. Arbitrary $S'$ is allowed by the cited small-site and descent results.

source.place: Remarks 0E46 and 0E47, composition of ordinary base-change maps; spaces-simplicial.tex Tag 0D99.

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q30-3687bfc61 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's statement, all 7 steps and every field, the new node lem-trf-total-site-augmentation-spectral-sequence in full, the statements of all cited nodes, and the parent's uses of the item. Read at the cited places in local Stacks spaces-simplicial.tex: 0D99, 0DH1 with lemma-morphism-simplicial-sites-modules, 0D7F with its double-complex proof and lemma-augmentation-cech-complex-modules, 0DHL; also homology lemma-first-quadrant-ss and 0E46/0E47. The Orgogozo PDF is WANTED and proof_origin is honestly by: agent. The item statement is unchanged and keeps every hypothesis. Its coefficients are constant-Λ modules on the small étale and vanishing topoi, matching the descent lemma.

The route is correct. Ordinary proper hyperdescent gives K≅Rε_*ε^*K. Applying Rψ_{f,*} and derived composition along ε̄ψ_•≅ψ_fε gives RΨ_fK≅Rε̄_*L with L=Rψ_{•,*}ε^*K. The components of L are r_iL≅RΨ_{f_i}K_i, and the lower bound c holds by left t-exactness and conservativity of the restrictions. The general-site spectral sequence then gives E1^{i,j}=H^j(Rε̄_{i,*}RΨ_{f_i}K_i), with i≥0, j≥c, and graded pieces for 0≤i≤n−c. Tested on the identity hypercover (E2 concentrated in column 0), on K=0, on negative c, and on n<c.

The new node is true for geometric transition morphisms with constant Λ: g_{p!} is exact, components of direct images are componentwise, the 0D7F argument shifts by c, and functoriality comes from a map of double complexes built from base-change maps. It is a needed generalization of lem-trf-simplicial-derived-image-spectral-sequence, which covers only étale sites of simplicial schemes, and vanishing topoi are not such sites. Its module component clauses overlap the abelian-sheaf nodes lem-trf-total-site-component-restriction and lem-trf-total-site-derived-components; I accepted the overlap and noted it for the future split.

Two fixes. (1) In the new node, the component identification is now stated as the canonical base-change map r_pRh_*J→Rh_{p,*}r'_pJ, the mate of h_p^*r_p≃r'_ph^*, which is an isomorphism, exactly as in 0DH1. The node also states r'_ph^*≃h_p^*r_p and cites def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object. (2) In item step 7, I added the justification that the component of the total comparison w^*L→L' is β for Y_i, by mate pasting (clauses 1–2) with those base-change squares.
